title: Contract Metadata and Catalog
description: The control-plane contract: it describes the catalog document that registers every published contract, and the shape of a single catalog entry. Unlike the interface envelopes, this schema is closed - an unrecognised key is a mistake in the catalog, not a forward-compatible addition, and must fail validation rather than be ignored.

catalog_version.title: Catalog document version
catalog_version.description: Semantic version of the catalog document itself, distinct from the version of any contract it registers.

contracts.title: Registered contracts
contracts.description: Every published contract. The (contract_id, version) pair must be unique across this array; duplicates are rejected by catalog validation.

repository.title: Platform repository
repository.description: One of the eight independently versioned platform repositories. The closed list is deliberate: an owner or consumer outside it means the entry is wrong, or the platform topology changed and this contract must change with it.

semver.title: Semantic version
semver.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with no pre-release or build metadata. Released versions are immutable; a correction is a new version.

contract_entry.title: Catalog entry
contract_entry.description: One published contract. Ownership is singular and mandatory: a contract without exactly one owner is invalid.

contract_id.title: Stable contract identifier
contract_id.description: URN that stays constant across compatible versions. The trailing v<major> marks the generation, so incompatible generations coexist under distinct identifiers.

type.title: Contract family
type.description: The artifact family, which determines how the source file is validated.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle state
lifecycle.description: draft: not yet consumable. active: published and supported. deprecated: still supported, replacement announced, carries deprecation metadata. retired: no longer supported.

owner.title: Authoritative owner
owner.description: The single repository with authority over this contract's shape, version, and deprecation. Exactly one, always.

consumers.title: Declared consumers
consumers.description: Repositories that depend on this contract. Listed explicitly so consumer impact is a fact rather than a guess when a change is proposed. May be empty for a contract nothing consumes yet.

source.title: Canonical source path
source.description: Repository-relative path to the contract source. Must resolve to a file that exists, so the catalog cannot drift from the tree.

compatibility.title: Compatibility mode
compatibility.description: backward: new versions accept data written for old ones. forward: old versions accept data written for new ones. full: both. none: no guarantee, permitted only for draft contracts.

description.title: Human-readable summary
description.description: One line describing what the contract governs. Documentation only; not a compatibility key.

deprecation.title: Deprecation metadata
deprecation.description: Required once lifecycle is deprecated or retired, and meaningless before then. Names the replacement and the earliest retirement date so consumers can plan.

deprecated_at.description: Date the contract entered deprecated state, as an RFC 3339 full-date.

replaced_by.description: contract_id of the replacement, or omitted if the capability is withdrawn entirely.

earliest_retirement.description: Earliest date the contract may move to retired, as an RFC 3339 full-date.
